items.title: What is the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)?
items.summary: What is the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)? Cyber Resilience Act What is the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA)? The Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) is a European Union regulation that establishes mandatory cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements, including hardware, software, and connected devices. The CRA aims to ensure products are secure by design, supported throughout their lifecycle, and better protected against evolving cyber threats. Why CRA Matters The growing number of connected products has increased the need for stronger cybersecurity protections. The Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) helps address this challenge by establishing common cybersecurity requirements for products with digital elements placed on the EU market. The regulation improves transparency, strengthens product security throughout the lifecycle, and helps organizations and consumers make more informed technology decisions. Proliferation of Connected Products Billions of devices across industries and homes Growing Cyber Threats Real-world attacks exploiting unpatched and insecure products Market Gaps Inconsistent security, no transparency, limited lifecycle support Regulatory Response The EU Cyber Resilience Act establishes mandatory cybersecurity requirements EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) Timeline The Cyber Resilience Act is being introduced in stages, with key milestones leading up to full applicability in December 2027. The timeline below outlines the major dates organizations should be aware of as they prepare for CRA compliance. CRA Scope – What Is Covered? CRA Scope – What Is Covered? The Cyber Resilience Act applies to a broad range of products with digital elements, including hardware, software, components, and certain remote services. While many connected products fall within the scope of the regulation, some categories—such as standalone cloud or SaaS services, non-commercial open-source software, products covered by equivalent sector regulations, and other exclusions defined by EU legislation—are not subject to CRA requirements. Hardware SoCs & Processors Microcontrollers IoT Devices Network Equipment Consumer Electronics Industrial Devices Software Firmware Operating Systems Applications Middleware Security Software Embedded Software Components Hardware Components Software Components Firmware Modules Embedded Modules Components Remote Data Processing Solutions (covered when necessary for the product to perform one or more of its intended functions) Both final products and their components are in scope. Hardware and software components are considered Products with Digital Elements (PDE) under the CRA. Secure Biometric Authentication Secure fingerprint sensors engineered for speed and accuracy. Hardware-based authentication replaces passwords with seamless, enterprise-grade protection—enabling fast login and trusted security across modern notebook designs. Standalone Cloud / SaaS Pure cloud services or SaaS offerings not necessary for the product to perform its intended functions. Non-commercial Open Source Free and open-source software projects not supplied in the course of a commercial activity. Equivalent Sector Regulations Medical Devices, Automotive, Civil Aviation, and Maritime products and systems. Other Exclusions Defined by EU Legislation If specific products are sufficiently covered by existing EU cybersecurity legislation. CRA Applicability – New vs. Existing Products CRA Applicability – New vs. Existing Products Which Products does the CRA apply to? Starting December 11, 2027 , new products with digital elements placed on the EU market must comply with the Cyber Resilience Act. Products already on the market before that date are generally exempt unless they undergo a substantial modification that impacts cybersecurity requirements or changes the product's intended purpose. When significant changes are made, a compliance reassessment may be required.
